title: Exceptional Gender Categories
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 42; Ryding Ch. 6)
objectives: Identify unmarked feminine nouns (al-muʾannath al-samāʿī): paired body parts, elemental nouns, and cities/tribes.
Recognize nouns of common gender (treated as either masculine or feminine, e.g., طَرِيقٌ, سَبِيلٌ, حَالٌ).
Identify feminine markers beyond ة: alif maqṣūrah (ـى, e.g., كُبْرَى) and alif mamdūdah (ـَاءُ, e.g., صَحْرَاءُ).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 3: Name two unmarked feminine nouns learned in Module 1.

sections.heading: Beyond Tāʾ Marbūṭah
sections.body: Besides tāʾ marbūṭah (ة), Arabic has two other feminine markers—alif maqṣūrah (ـى, as in كُبْرَى 'greatest f.') and alif mamdūdah (ـَاءُ, as in صَحْرَاءُ 'desert')—both of which make the word a diptote. Furthermore, many nouns are grammatically feminine by classical usage (samāʿī) without any marker.

sections.label: Unmarked Feminine Categories
sections.summary: Always feminine without ة: (1) paired body parts (يَدٌ 'hand', عَيْنٌ 'eye', رِجْلٌ 'foot', أُذُنٌ 'ear'); (2) elemental/cosmic nouns (شَمْسٌ, أَرْضٌ, نَارٌ, رِيحٌ, نَفْسٌ); (3) names of cities, lands, and tribes (مَكَّةُ, مِصْرُ, قُرَيْشٌ).

sections.irab: النَّفْسُ: مُؤَنَّثٌ سَمَاعِيٌّ مَرْفُوعٌ | المُطْمَئِنَّةُ: نَعْتٌ مَرْفُوعٌ مُؤَنَّثٌ
sections.notes: نَفْسٌ ('soul/self') has no ة, yet it is feminine by usage, so its adjective المُطْمَئِنَّةُ takes ة.

sections.heading: Singular Body Parts
sections.body: While paired body parts (يَدٌ, عَيْنٌ) are feminine, single body parts (رَأْسٌ 'head', قَلْبٌ 'heart', لِسَانٌ 'tongue') are masculine.
